entries.reason: iOS 6 has none of it: the release's private CMSampleBufferCallForEachSample is a different function with a different contract, and this one is written over the public block buffer and sample timing the release does carry
entries.effect: walks the sample buffer's own sample sizes and per-sample timing, builds a one-sample buffer over each sample's bytes with CMBlockBufferCreateWithBufferReference, hands it to the block with its index, and stops at the first error the block returns; a buffer with no sample sizes is kCMSampleBufferError_CannotSubdivide, and a sample whose timing the release cannot report gives the release's own kCMSampleBufferError_BufferHasNoSampleTimingInfo

entries.reason: the block-taking form of CMSampleBufferCreate arrived at 12.2; iOS 6's CMSampleBuffer is a system object with nowhere to keep a block
entries.effect: builds the buffer with the release's own CMSampleBufferCreate at the readiness asked for and, when it was not ready, runs the handler over the finished buffer, answering the handler's own status; a failure releases the buffer and leaves the out parameter null. The handler runs during this call, before it returns, and the port does not register it with the release, so a second CMSampleBufferMakeDataReady is the release's own and does not run it again
entries.source: the host's own CoreMedia, held case by case over 239 answers by tests/backports/host/coremedia7/createready.m: 179 inside the claim with none different, 60 outside it with 58 the same

entries.reason: corpus row 5186, demand rank 192 with LOAD-FAIL for one application: a program that does not load without it; the field it reads is mVariableFramesInPacket, which Apple's CoreAudioTypes declares in every SDK the port builds against, and a previous delivery left it out on a false premise that the type is incomplete
entries.effect: lays the sample buffer out from the packet descriptions and hands it to the release's own CMSampleBufferCreate as one timing entry and one sizing entry, the 'every sample is the same' form Apple's header describes: the duration is the stream's mFramesPerPacket at its mSampleRate, the size is the description's mDataByteSize or the stream's mFramesPerPacket times its per-frame bytes; zero samples is kCMSampleBufferError_InvalidEntryCount, a presentation timestamp that is not numeric is kCMSampleBufferError_SampleTimingInfoInvalid, and with no packet descriptions a format with no per-frame byte size at all is kCMSampleBufferError_RequiredParameterMissing
entries.source: the host's own CoreMedia, held case by case over 239 answers by tests/backports/host/coremedia7/createready.m; the three field names read from CoreAudioBaseTypes.h in the iPhoneOS 16.4 SDK the gate resolves, iPhoneOS 26.2 and the macOS SDK alike
